title: Lower projection remains degreewise epic under compatible upper truncation
statement: Let $C$ be an abelian category, $K$ a cochain complex indexed by $\mathbb Z$, and $a,t\in\mathbb Z$ with $a\le t$. Write $\tau_{\ge a}$ and $\tau_{\le t}$ for canonical smart truncations: the former replaces degree $a$ by the cokernel of the incoming differential, and the latter replaces degree $t$ by the kernel of the outgoing differential, with zero objects outside their indicated ranges. The map $\tau_{\le t}(K\to\tau_{\ge a}K)$ is an epimorphism in every degree.

source.place: homology-section-truncations, cochain canonical truncations (3) and (4); specialization of the assigned node's endpoint argument.

proof.text: Above t the target is zero. Below t both upper inclusion components are invertible; naturality transports the epic lower projection to the asserted component. In Lean this uses inclusion_f_isIso and HomologicalComplex.ιTruncLE_naturality.

At t identify the upper cutoff objects with cycles. If a<t, the lower projection is invertible in degrees t and t+1; Mathlib ShortComplex.isIso_cyclesMap_of_isIso_of_mono makes the cycles map invertible. If a=t, the lower truncation has zero incoming differential, so its homology projection is invertible. The lower projection is a quasi-isomorphism in degree a. Naturality of homology and epi_comp_iff_of_isIso show that the cycles map is epic. Conjugate by the upper-boundary cycles identifications. These arguments are fully formalized in this module. Reuse the existing private CochainComplex.pi_f_above from LowerTruncationTransitionKernel and CochainComplex.truncLEXIsoCycles_naturality from UpperTruncationStepSES through proof-only import all. The latter already uses truncLEXIsoCycles_comp_iCycles; none of these three facts is redeclared here.
